commit.message:
Let line break rules decide the break at the end of a complex run (#8574)

## Summary

Fixes #7218. Fixes #8243.

The V1 and V3 line segmenters return the dictionary/LSTM breakpoint at
the end
of a complex (SA) run as is, which bypasses the UAX #14 rules for the
pair of
characters around the run end. This gives breaks before closing
punctuation,
spaces and other characters that must not start a line:

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `ไทย!` | `ไทย\|!` | `ไทย!` |
| `แดง (อังกฤษ: Red` | `แดง\| \|(อังกฤษ\|: \|Red` | `แดง \|(อังกฤษ:
\|Red` |
| `“ไทย”` | `“ไทย\|”` | `“ไทย”` |
| `ລາວ! ລາວ` | `ລາວ\|! \|ລາວ` | `ລາວ! \|ລາວ` |

Following @makotokato's suggestion in #7232, the iterator now stops on
the last
character of the run and lets the rule table decide the boundary with
the
following character, where SA resolves to AL. Breaks inside the run are
unchanged. This is about 20 lines each in `line/v1.rs` and `line/v3.rs`,
with no
hard-coded character lists.

The fall-through has to happen on every `None` from the complex handler,
not
only when the iterator moved. Otherwise V3 breaks a two-code-point run
ending in
a combining mark (`ปี` → `ป|ี`), because V3 skips LB9 for SA × SA_MC_MN.

The #7218 and #8243 inputs now pass on V1/17, so `V1_17_KNOWN_FAILURES`
is
empty. The ill-formed UTF-8/UTF-16 expectations in
`complex_line_break_encodings` now match
`complex_line_break_encodings_neo`.
A new test, `complex_run_end_follows_rules`, covers punctuation, spaces,
ZWSP,
NBSP, newlines and Lao on V1/V3 with dictionary and LSTM.

Notes for review:
- Thai directly followed by Latin letters or digits (`ไทยabc`, `ไทย123`)
no
longer breaks at the script boundary (LB28/LB23). This matches V2 and
UAX #14.
- Breaks before `ๆ`/`ฯ` come from the LSTM output itself and are not
addressed
  here.

## Changelog

icu_segmenter: Fix line breaks at the end of Southeast Asian (SA) runs
in the V1 and V3 line segmenters
- Breaks at the end of Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar runs now follow the
UAX #14
rules, so lines no longer break before closing punctuation, spaces, or a
word joiner.
- Thai directly followed by Latin letters or digits no longer breaks,
matching V2.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Reduce allocations for complex segmenter runs (#8144)

## Changelog

Performance: Avoid temporary complex-run input allocations in the
published word and line segmenters.

## Summary

The V1 word and line segmenters previously copied every complex-script
run into a temporary `String` or `Vec<u16>` before dictionary or LSTM
segmentation. This keeps one original `Y::IterAttr` and slices it by the
run's absolute offsets instead.

This is encoding-generic rather than a `str` specialization:

- `Utf8` slices `CharIndices::as_str()` with byte offsets.
- `PotentiallyIllFormedUtf8` slices `Utf8CharIndices::as_slice()` with
byte offsets.
- `Utf16` slices `Utf16Indices::as_slice()` with code unit offsets.

Potentially ill-formed UTF-8 is passed through the byte-based complex
segmenter, where `Utf8CharIndices` preserves replacement-character
semantics. UTF-16 continues to preserve unpaired surrogates in the outer
rule iterator. The implementation covers published word segmentation and
both V1 and V3 line segmentation; the V2/neo path already slices
`Y::IterAttr` directly.

No public API changes are introduced.

## Performance

Baseline: `origin/main` at `72bbff74dc`. Current: `33a4116e38`.

The representative workloads and dictionary constructors come from the
merged segmenter benchmarks: `Ja` for word segmentation and `Th` for
line segmentation. The baseline includes the result-cache consumption
optimization from #8143. A matching local probe covers raw
`segment_utf8`, which is not currently included in the Criterion
harness, and reports allocations per complete segmentation call. Probe
times are medians of three alternating baseline/current release runs
with 1,000 warm-up calls and 250,000 measured calls.

| Workload | Allocations before | Allocations after | Bytes before |
Bytes after | Time before | Time after | Time delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| word `segment_str` / Ja | 8 | 3 | 472 | 224 | 1.520 us | 1.359 us |
-10.6% |
| word `segment_utf8` / Ja | 8 | 3 | 472 | 224 | 1.631 us | 1.581 us |
-3.1% |
| word `segment_utf16` / Ja | 9 | 3 | 474 | 224 | 1.431 us | 1.265 us |
-11.6% |
| line `segment_str` / Th | 30 | 6 | 912 | 192 | 2.711 us | 2.010 us |
-25.9% |
| line `segment_utf8` / Th | 30 | 6 | 912 | 192 | 2.934 us | 2.446 us |
-16.6% |
| line `segment_utf16` / Th | 30 | 6 | 540 | 192 | 2.295 us | 1.781 us |
-22.4% |

The merged Criterion harness independently reports:

| Criterion case | Before | After | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Word Break/UTF8/Ja/dictionary | 1.468 us | 1.331 us | -9.3% |
| Word Break/UTF16/Ja/dictionary | 1.423 us | 1.296 us | -8.9% |
| Line Break/UTF8/Th/dictionary | 2.621 us | 1.981 us | -24.4% |
| Line Break/UTF16/Th/dictionary | 2.312 us | 1.852 us | -19.9% |

The cache stress benchmarks added by #8143 confirm that the two
optimizations compose:

| Criterion case, 16K chars | Before | After | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Full word segmentation, continuous Han | 857.4 us | 483.2 us | -43.6%
|
| Full line segmentation, continuous Thai | 342.9 us | 335.6 us | -2.1%
|
| First 10 word boundaries, continuous Han | 817.2 us | 457.8 us |
-44.0% |
| First 10 line boundaries, continuous Thai | 321.6 us | 309.8 us |
-3.7% |

commit.message:
Optimize segmenter result cache consumption (#8143)

This PR removes the repeated allocation performed when the v1
complex-break cache consumes a boundary.

## Design

Complex-run-relative offsets are converted once into distances between
adjacent breaks. The cache keeps natural order in
`vec::IntoIter<usize>`: `as_slice().first()` peeks at the next distance
and `next()` consumes it in O(1).

This follows the v2/neo cache representation and addresses the review
feedback directly: there is no reversed vector, `Vec + index` state, or
per-boundary offset compensation. Public API and segmentation behavior
are unchanged.

## Performance

Measured on an Apple M4 Max, comparing `main@3f2215305` with
`PR@7a5fdbc4c`.

| 1M-character full traversal | main | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Word dictionary, continuous Han | 19.063 s | 31.859 ms (598x) |
| Line dictionary, continuous Thai | 6.576 s | 22.834 ms (288x) |

At 1M characters, allocation calls and cumulative requested bytes drop
from `524,325 / 1.10 TB` to `38 / 16.8 MB` for word/Han, and from
`299,630 / 359 GB` to `38 / 16.8 MB` for line/Thai. Stopping after 10
boundaries remains neutral.

The merged PR #8141 workloads show the same direction on cache-heavy
paths:

- Thai line: LSTM `-5.4%`, dictionary `-7.1%`
- Japanese/Han word: auto neutral, dictionary `-15.0%`
- Mixed: line LSTM `-8.5%`, line dictionary `-2.4%`, word dictionary
`-10.8%`

Mixed word auto is about `+4%` in the latest paired rerun; it is a small
non-dictionary workload and remains the observed residual regression.

```sh
ICU4X_SEGMENTER_BENCH_LARGE=1 cargo bench -p icu_segmenter --bench bench -- "Complex Break Cache" --noplot
```

Validation: `cargo test -p icu_segmenter --features unstable` and Clippy
with `-D warnings` pass.

## Changelog (N/A)
